questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid name for a rectangle with corners labeled A, B, C, and D?
choices: ACBD
BCAD
ABDC
CDAB
questions.solution: The correct answer is ABDC because a valid name for a rectangle must follow the order of the corners as they appear around the rectangle. ABDC skips a corner and does not follow the correct order. ABCD, BCDA, and CDAB are all valid names as they follow the correct sequence of corners around the rectangle.

hi.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक आयत का वैध नाम नहीं है जिसके कोने A, B, C और D अंकित हैं?

hi.solution: सही उत्तर ABDC है क्योंकि एक आयत का वैध नाम कोनों के क्रम का अनुसरण करना चाहिए जैसा कि आयत के चारों ओर वे आते हैं। ABDC एक कोना छोड़ देता है और सही क्रम का अनुसरण नहीं करता है। ABCD, BCDA और CDAB सभी सही क्रम में कोनों के अनुक्रम का अनुसरण करते हैं और आयत के लिए वैध नाम हैं।

questions.stem: A rectangle is constructed with sides of 4 cm and 6 cm. Which of the following properties must it satisfy?
choices: All sides are equal
All angles are 60°
All angles are 90°
Opposite sides are not equal
questions.solution: A rectangle is defined as a quadrilateral with all angles equal to 90° and opposite sides equal. The correct option is that all angles are 90°. A square has all sides equal, so the first option is wrong. A 60° angle would make it a different shape, so the second option is incorrect. The last option contradicts the definition of a rectangle.

hi.solution: एक आयत की परिभाषा एक चतुर्भुज है जिसके सभी कोण 90° होते हैं और विपरीत भुजाएं समान होती हैं। सही विकल्प यह है कि सभी कोण 90° हैं। एक वर्ग में सभी भुजाएं समान होती हैं, इसलिए पहला विकल्प गलत है। 60° का कोण इसे एक अलग आकृति बना देगा, इसलिए दूसरा विकल्प गलत है। आखिरी विकल्प आयत की परिभाषा के विरोधी है।

mr.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate Marathi technical terms for geometry.

questions.stem: How can the fourth point of a rectangle be located if three points are already known?
choices: By drawing a straight line between the three known points
By drawing perpendiculars from the known points and finding their intersection
By measuring the length of each side and matching them
By using a protractor to measure angles and completing the shape
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'By drawing perpendiculars from the known points and finding their intersection'. This is because rectangles have right angles, and the fourth point can be found by drawing perpendiculars from the known points and seeing where they meet. Drawing a straight line between known points or using a protractor is not the most accurate method. Measuring side lengths to match them is not the correct approach as it does not ensure right angles.

choices: Using a ruler to measure distances

Using a ruler or a protractor is less precise, and drawing perpendicular lines from all sides is not the main technique.

questions.stem: How can point B be located in the construction of a rectangle with a base of 5 cm and a diagonal of 7 cm?
choices: By drawing a perpendicular to DC at point C
By drawing a circle of radius 7 cm with point D as the centre
By drawing a line through A perpendicular to AB

questions.solution: By drawing a circle of radius 7 cm with point D as the centre, point B can be located because the diagonal of the rectangle is 7 cm, and the circle will intersect the line where point B is situated. The other options either describe steps that are not directly related to locating point B or involve actions that do not use the diagonal length.

questions.stem: How can point A be located in the construction of a house with all sides of 5 cm?
choices: By drawing a line segment of 5 cm
By drawing a perpendicular from point D
By drawing two circles with radius 5 cm from points B and C
By drawing a diagonal of 7 cm
questions.solution: By drawing two circles with radius 5 cm from points B and C, the intersection of these circles will locate point A, as this method ensures equal distance from both points. Drawing a line segment of 5 cm only creates a straight line, not a specific point. A perpendicular from point D would not necessarily locate point A. A diagonal of 7 cm does not match the required 5 cm side length.

questions.stem: Can a 4-sided figure have all sides equal but not be a square?
choices: Yes, it can be a rectangle
Yes, it can be a rhombus
No, it cannot exist
Yes, it can be a trapezium
questions.solution: A rhombus is a 4-sided figure with all sides equal but not all angles equal to 90°, so it is not a square. A rectangle has all angles equal to 90°, but not all sides equal. A trapezium does not have all sides equal. The correct answer is that it can be a rhombus.
